newsitem.title: UK: Hermes sees Liberty venture as perfect fit.
newsitem.headline: Hermes sees Liberty venture as perfect fit.

text.p: British pension fund management group Hermes said on Thursday the joint pensions venture announced earlier with financial services and property group Liberty International Holdings was a meeting of minds.

"Liberty has the ability and techniques of selling pensions, it also has the systems...and the administration. We on the other hand are good at our particular core areas of investment management...we think that's a very good marriage," Alastair Ross Goobey, chief executive of Hermes, told Reuters.
Ross Goobey said there was no conflict of interest in the venture. Hermes had approached Liberty International only to find the group had been considering an approach to Hermes.
"It really was a meeting of minds on this. Whether it develops further from this we shall see. I think one step at a time is quite enough for us," Ross Goobey said.
He said the venture would probably not be up and running until the first quarter of next year as regulatory approval had to be obtained for the new group.

The decision by the giant British Telecom Pension Scheme to transfer 1.5 billion stg of assets to the new Hermes Liberty International Pensions funds should give the new venture a boost, Ross Goobey said.
"I would hope it gives some people some feeling of security that BT Pension Scheme, which is after all the biggest in the country, is willing to do this," he said.

"We have gone to a great deal of trouble to make sure the (BT Pension Scheme) assets are secure and still under Hermes' control so that the pension scheme is absolutely as secure as it was," Ross Goobey added.

Ross Goobey said that with more than 300 billion stg of pensions funds in the UK, there was a trend towards indexing part of portfolios, a service offered by the new venture, as active performance had not been particularly good.
There was also a whole new phase of personal pensions and defined contribution schemes underway and Hermes would have to capture its share of new forms of pensions savings.
"We've got to make sure our product is competitive and performs well," he said.
